subject: ACME POC: Eval methodology & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>, Tom Andrews <tom.andrews@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: ACME POC: Eval methodology & success criteria

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped and started:

1) Success criteria (your input required):
   - Latency: 95th percentile < 300ms for 1-2k daily active users
   - Qualitative: pass rate >= 85% on safety/regression rubric for the 200 sample prompts
   - Cost: token cost target < $0.004 per token (approx)

2) Evaluation approach options (we should pick one):
   - Offline evals: we run an offline benchmark on the 200 prompt set you shared. Grading is performed by ACME SMEs against a rubric (accuracy, relevance, hallucination, safety). Iterative tuning possible between runs.
   - Online shadow: Redwood runs models in shadow for 1 week in your staging traffic. We collect online metrics and human-review a stratified sample. Better for signal on production distribution but takes longer and requires staging integration.

3) Proposed timeline:
   - Week 1: Finalize success criteria + rubric (owner: ACME + Redwood)
   - Week 2: Offline run (if chosen) and feedback loop
   - Week 3: Optional online shadow run and sample grading

4) Ownership / next steps:
   - ACME: finalize rubric and confirm priority prompt subsets (Lisa/Tom)
   - Redwood: provide eval plan + initial run, share results and recommendations (Marissa/Dylan)

Action requested: Please confirm which evaluation approach you prefer and any edits to the success criteria by EOD Tuesday (2027-04-27). I attached a draft eval plan (v1) for reference - will upload v2 after your feedback.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Andrews <tom.andrews@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME POC: Eval methodology & success criteria

Marissa - thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick questions from our side:

- For the offline eval, can you propose a grading rubric template we can review? We want the rubric to include explicit checks for hallucination and compliance with our content policy.
- For the online shadow option, what are the staging integration requirements? Is there anything we need to provision on our side beyond a staging key and sample traffic routing?

We prefer to start with offline evals to get quick signal, then consider a short shadow run. Also, small request: could you break down the 200 prompts into these buckets: transactional (40%), support (40%), marketing/product (20%)? That will help our SMEs prioritize reviews.

Thanks - Lisa
Lisa Chen
Product Lead, Conversational AI
ACME Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>, Tom Andrews <tom.andrews@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME POC: Eval methodology & success criteria

Perfect - thanks for the direction, Lisa. Attach: acme-eval-plan-v2.pdf (updated rubric + prompt buckets). Summary of what we changed based on your note:

- Rubric template included: numeric scales (0-3) for Relevance, Accuracy, Hallucination (binary flag + severity), Safety/Policy compliance, and Response Completeness. Aggregate pass if average >= 2.5 and no severe hallucination flags.
- Prompt buckets added per your split (transactional/support/marketing).
- Offline run estimate: 48 hours to process and generate human review packets; SME review depends on ACME bandwidth (we estimate 4-8 hours per SME for 200 prompts).
- Staging requirements for shadow: a staging API key, ability to route a 5% sampling rule from staging traffic to Redwood shadow endpoint, and a non-production dataset flag for telemetry. We can provide Terraform snippets to make this trivial.

Next steps:
- Lisa/Tom: confirm rubric and SME reviewers by EOD Tue (2027-04-27)
- Dylan: will schedule the offline run and share the runbook.

Marissa
